claim: #579 AC3 — 'F20 recaptured; strict manifest quality gate green'
note: The strict manifest quality gate does not exit 0, and this record does not restate it as though it did. It exits 1 on exactly 12 defects, every one of which pre-dates this batch and none of which this batch's cascade can reach. The owner ruled (ruling B, binding, 2026-08-14) that those 12 are recorded-and-accepted and that AC3 closes green-modulo-those-12. The defects below were re-measured by running the gate at this working tree — not copied from the ruling — and each class is explained by an independent measurement of the thing the gate is complaining about, so a reader can tell a stale citation from a real regression without re-deriving it.

ownerRuling.effect: The 12 defects enumerated below are recorded-and-accepted and are outside #579's cascade. AC3 closes green-modulo-those-12. The parent rows that carry the defects are NOT to be edited by this batch.
ownerRuling.parentRowsEditedEvidence: This record is a sibling artifact under docs/exec-plans/evidence/. Neither canonical-v1-goal-task-manifest-v1.json nor canonical-v1-watcher-dependency-map-v1.json was modified to satisfy AC3; the gate output quoted below is what the unmodified tree produces.

gate.name: goal:tasks:quality:verify
gate.exitSemantics: demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-goal-task-manifest-quality.mjs:1583 — `process.exit(summary.defects === 0 ? 0 : 1)`. Exit 1 means defects > 0; it is not a crash. Exit 2 is the usage error, which is what a `--strict` flag produces: the gate has no `--strict` mode, it is strict unconditionally, so 'the strict manifest quality gate' names this gate's only mode rather than a flag.

defectSetMatchEvidence: The gate emitted 12 defects in 2 categories with the exact ids and details the ruling enumerates: 9 unresolvableFocusedModuleCitation at ids C20-0..C20-8 all naming `midgard/fraud_proofs/proof_v1_fragment_envelope.test`, and 3 watcherFocusedGateContractMismatch all reporting a 616 claim against a 617 requirement. No defect outside the enumeration appeared, and no enumerated defect was absent.

defectClasses.emittedDetail: midgard/fraud_proofs/proof_v1_fragment_envelope.test names no Aiken module under onchain/aiken/lib or onchain/aiken/validators
defectClasses.carriedBy: docs/exec-plans/evidence/canonical-v1-goal-task-manifest-v1.json — the nine C20-* task rows, one per transaction field: C20-0 field 0 spend inputs, C20-1 field 1 reference inputs, C20-2 field 2 outputs, C20-3 field 3 observers, C20-4 field 4 required signers, C20-5 field 5 mint/burn, C20-6 field 6 script witnesses, C20-7 field 7 vkey witnesses, C20-8 field 8 redeemer item descriptor.
defectClasses.why: All nine rows carry the same focused-test citation because they are the nine arms of one family — the nine-field consumer — and the family was specified with a single shared focused-test module. That module was never written. This is a forward citation that never landed, not a rename that drifted: a search for the cited basename returns nothing under onchain/aiken/lib or onchain/aiken/validators, and there is no near-match to have drifted from — the only module in the tree with `envelope` in its name is onchain/aiken/validators/fraud-proofs/validation-trace/script-sources-stage-one-redeemer-envelope-v1.ak, a different family on a different door, and no `proof_v1*` module exists at all.
whyMeasuredBy: find onchain/aiken/lib onchain/aiken/validators -name '*fragment*' -o -name '*envelope*'  -> one unrelated file, script-sources-stage-one-redeemer-envelope-v1.ak
defectClasses.outsideCascadeBecause: #579's cascade regenerates onchain/aiken/plutus.json and reconciles the artifacts that quote it. Creating a missing Aiken test module — or retracting nine manifest citations — writes new test source and edits parent-owned manifest rows, neither of which regeneration reaches and both of which the ruling forbids this batch from doing.

emittedDetail.detail: source cardinality=20, dependency-map files=20, aggregate=617; expected exact 20/616

defectClasses.carriedBy: W25 (Phase B/block replay) and W26 (Event/classification verifier) are task rows in canonical-v1-goal-task-manifest-v1.json. `watcher-focused-gate` is not a task id — it is the gate's own synthetic id for the source-cardinality check it runs against demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-watcher-focused-tests.mjs, which is why this class has three members but only two manifest rows.
defectClasses.why: The watcher focused-gate contract is pinned in two places that have fallen one test apart. The authority is canonical-v1-watcher-dependency-map-v1.json, whose 20 per-file `expectedFocusedTestCount` values sum to 617. The manifest prose and the focused-gate script both still pin the older total of 616. The file cardinality is NOT in dispute — both sides say 20, and the map really does carry 20 counted files — so this is a one-test drift in the aggregate only, not a missing or extra test file.
whyMeasuredBy: Per-file counts measured: publicDaClient 102, phaseAVerifier 94, headerRootReconstruction 59, canonicalBlockStore 46, strictConfiguration 42, rollbackEngine 26, finalityEngine 25, settlementIndexer 25, userEventIndexer 24, l1Adapter 23, blockReplay 21, stateQueueIndexer 19, deploymentIdentity 18, multiProviderConsistency 18, proofThreadIndexer 17, crashRollbackMatrix 17, eventClassificationVerifier 15, durableStore 12, ruleBundle 9, scaffold 5.
defectClasses.outsideCascadeBecause: Closing this drift means moving the pinned 616 to 617 in the manifest rows and in demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-watcher-focused-tests.mjs together — the manifest itself records that those must move in one integration, and both are parent-owned. #579 regenerates the blueprint; it does not add, remove, or rename a watcher test, so nothing in this batch moved the count that drifted.

retirement.authorizedBy: #581 E-2/E-3 owner ruling (2026-08-16: 'file follow-up, land'), executed as the #613 coordinated six-surface re-pin.
retirement.arithmetic: This class was recorded as a 616-claim-vs-617-requirement offset. Before it was retired the true measured aggregate had moved again: commit 04aaae57 (#594) added two it() blocks to demo/midgard-watcher/tests/user-event-indexer.test.ts after the pins were last updated at df53dc6a (#587), so the suite collects 26 there against the pinned 24 (measured this re-pin: 'Vitest collected counts do not match the runner-measured pins: user-event-indexer.test.ts collected 26 against pin 24'). The re-pin therefore moved userEventIndexer.expectedFocusedTestCount 24 -> 26 (map aggregate 617 -> 619), the focused-gate pin table 24 -> 26 with pinnedTotal 617 -> 619, the quality gate's aggregate literal 616 -> 619, and every manifest aggregate claim 616 -> 619 (7 '616/616' and 12 '616-test' occurrences), in one commit. The predicted 616 -> 617 retirement in ac3Closure.howToRetireLater was written before #594 landed; 619 is the measured total it became.

acceptedDefectsAfter613Repin.note: Standing enumeration for gates built after the #613 re-pin (e.g. the #614 CI allowlist): the accepted defect set is now exactly the 9 unresolvableFocusedModuleCitation defects at C20-0..C20-8. The 3 watcherFocusedGateContractMismatch defects recorded above were retired by the #613 six-surface re-pin and are preserved above only as the measured history of ruling B's original 12.

ac3Closure.residualRisk: Both classes are citation drift in the manifest's own bookkeeping, not a claim about compiled or deployed behaviour. Neither class can mask a regression introduced by this batch: the 9 unresolvable citations point at a module that has never existed at any revision, and the watcher mismatch is a fixed one-test offset between two pins that this batch does not write. A NEW defect in either category, or any defect in a third category, would change the count off 12 and fail this record's own equality check.
ac3Closure.howToRetireLater: Retiring these is a parent integration, not a follow-up to #579: either write the cited focused-test module or retract the nine C20-* citations, and move the watcher pin 616 -> 617 in the manifest rows and the focused-gate script in the same change.
